2609.03213.title: LLMs Learn Better In-Context from Rules than from Examples
2609.03213.paper_summary: Large language models (LLMs) exhibit in-context learning capabilities, where they can learn new tasks from prompt contexts without weight updates. We compare the learning efficacies of two prominent modes of in-context learning: (1) learning from descriptions of rules (instruction following); and (2) learning from examples of input-output demonstrations (few-shot prompting). Through five learning tasks that cover diverse domains (games, arithmetic, linguistic inferences), we compare two modes of learning (rules vs. examples) specifying the same underlying task. We furthermore explore model and task properties that modulate the learning efficacies. We find that models generally learn more reliably from rules than from examples alone, and additional examples on top of rules or simply scaling up the number of examples do not lead to consistent and significant gains. Instruction tuning amplifies the benefit of rule-based learning while keeping example-based learning capacities intact. Surprisingly, we find no privileged effect of example-based learning in base models, and rules still lead to gains in algebraic task domains. Overall, the comparative efficacy of rules over examples is larger when the task recruits algebraic abstractions and computations, and smaller when the task requires distributional sensitivity and/or recruits parametric knowledge.
2609.03213.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLMs）展現了上下文學習的能力，能夠在不更新權重的情況下從提示上下文中學習新任務。我們比較了兩種主要的上下文學習模式的學習效率：（1）從規則描述中學習（遵循指示）；以及（2）從輸入輸出示範的例子中學習（少量提示）。通過五個涵蓋不同領域（遊戲、算術、語言推理）的學習任務，我們比較了兩種學習模式（規則與例子），這些模式指定了相同的基本任務。我們進一步探討了調節學習效率的模型和任務特性。我們發現模型通常從規則中學習的可靠性高於僅從例子中學習，並且在規則基礎上增加額外的例子或僅僅擴大例子的數量並不會帶來一致且顯著的增益。指令調整增強了基於規則學習的好處，同時保持了基於例子學習的能力。令人驚訝的是，我們發現在基礎模型中，基於例子的學習並沒有特別的效果，而規則仍然在代數任務領域中帶來增益。總體而言，當任務涉及代數抽象和計算時，規則相對於例子的比較效率更高，而當任務需要分佈敏感性和/或涉及參數知識時，則較小。
